newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Tractebel seen eager buy out Powerfin.
newsitem.headline: Tractebel seen eager buy out Powerfin.

text.p: Belgian holding company Tractebel SA is seen eager to buy out its Powerfin unit, but the operation could still be months away, Belgian analysts said.
Analysts think Tractebel, which holds 59.77 percent of Powerfin, is eager to get full ownership of Powerfin, which has spearheaded the group's ambitious foreign expansion plans.
Powerfin operates power plants in Northern Ireland, Portugal, the U.S., Germany, Hungary and Chili and has projects in many other countries, including Oman, Italy, India, Kazakhstand and Malaysia.

"If Tractebel merges with Powerfin, it does not have to share the fruits of Powerfin's investments with anyone else, then they have 100 percent of its growth prospects," said Maud Watelet of brokerage Mignon Hanart Declerck.

She added that Tractebel chief executive officer Philippe Bodson had always been reluctant to give information about Powerfin's foreign strategy. A delisting of Powerfin would allow Tractebel to be more discreet in that area.
Jurgen Fryges of KB Securities added that a merger would also make it easier for the group to raise capital for foreign expansion through Tractebel, rather than lesser-known Powerfin.
"A Tractebel-Powerfin merger has been on the cards for a long time, the only obstacle was that it would have diluted SGB's Tractebel stake," said BBL analyst Jean-Marie Louis.
A source close to Tractebel said that a Tractebel-Powerfin merger would dilute SGB's Tractebel stake to just over 50 percent, still a comfortable majority.
One analyst said Tractebel is unlikely to make a move towards Powerfin until after SGB's October 9-30 public offer for Tractebel closes.
